newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU 14 oil stocks rise in January. [CORRECTED 15:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: EU 14 oil stocks rise in January. [CORRECTED 15:05 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects figures throughout, due to a late revision of the gasoline, distillate and fuel oil stock figures for one of the EU 14 countries)

Crude and oil product stocks in 14 countries of the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose by 5.90 million barrels, or 0.6 percent, in January to 1,031.36 million barrels, Stichting Euroilstock said in its latest monthly report.
The build left them 13.47 million barrels, or 1.3 percent, higher than in January 1996.
Crude oil stocks rose by 3.43 million barrels, or 0.9 percent, in January to 406.46 million barrels, leaving them 16.46 million barrels, or 4.2 percent, up on year-ago levels.
Middle distillate stocks fell by 4.57 million barrels, or 1.5 percent, to 293.93 million barrels, but were still 7.94 million barrels, or 2.8 percent, higher than a year ago.
Month-on-month, distillate stocks were stable in Germany.
Gasoline inventories were up 8.16 million barrels, or 5.2 percent, in January to 164.60 million barrels, but were 5.61 million barrels, or 3.3 percent, lower than a year ago.
Fuel oil stocks were 1.56 million barrels, or 1.1 percent, lower at 138.65 million barrels. This left a year-on-year shortfall of 5.39 million barrels, or 3.7 percent.
Naphtha stocks rose 440,000 barrels to 27.72 million barrels.
Crude intake was 130,000 barrels per day (bpd) lower than in December at 11.510 million bpd, leading to a utilisation rate of 91.35 percent in January.
